core.title: Start likely-needed work early only when it is reversible and cannot change accepted behavior
core.given: Work that may be needed later is proposed or implemented to start before its need is confirmed (any cost, any phase)
core.when: the planner authors or reviews that step in a plan artifact, acceptance or documentation
core.then: Allow the speculative work only if it is reversible and discarding or cancelling it cannot change accepted behavior.
prefer: Consider when expensive future work is predictable and wasted work can be budgeted.
Define isolation, cancellation and resource budgets for the speculative work.
Test wrong predictions, cancellation races, duplicate attempts, isolation and total wasted work; measure net benefit.
avoid: Speculating authority commits, irreversible side effects, externally visible mutations or unauthorized data access.
Assuming a generic speculative journey scheduler exists or using this pattern to authorize undeclared execution.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior or a new runtime dispatch option from this pattern.
core.why: Speculation saves latency only if wrong guesses are harmless; work that commits authority, mutates visibly or is irreversible cannot be cleanly discarded and would change accepted behavior.
evidence: Isolation, cancellation and resource budgets are defined for each speculative step.
Wrong predictions, cancellation races, duplicate attempts, isolation and total wasted work are tested, and net benefit is measured.
No speculative step performs an authority commit, irreversible side effect, externally visible mutation or unauthorized data access.
The existing plan and source checks pass; the work relies only on declared runtime execution, not an assumed speculative scheduler.
verification: Guidance for agents, not independent enforcement; this rule has no dedicated detector. Compliance is reviewed through the stack's existing plan-artifact and source checks plus review of the plan or change.

Not covered by any check: speculative work already implemented in a change has no observer; detecting it in a diff would need a new diff-level observer, so implementation-side compliance relies on review.

values: work is started before its need is confirmed (proposed in a plan artifact, acceptance or documentation, or already implemented)

fires: A plan proposes precomputing or prefetching results before the upstream step confirms they are needed.
A plan artifact proposes to start a likely next journey step in parallel and discard it if the prediction is wrong.
Speculative work (cheap or expensive) is introduced or found during implementation and must be planned or reviewed for reversibility.
A cheap early-start step would perform an externally visible mutation or authority commit.
doesNotFire: A plan that executes steps only after its trigger is confirmed (no early or predicted work).
Plans that only reference existing, declared runtime dispatch options without introducing early/predicted work.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds of the stack, so that the core's 'plan artifact' covers every artifact in which the planner may author or review a speculative step.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a journey-planning behavior pattern with no stack mechanics, so almost every field carried over verbatim and bunOnly is empty. The only stack-specific tokens were the plan-artifact kind names 'product capability' and 'DESIRED OUTCOME' (in when and activation.facts[1]); the core says 'plan artifact' and takes the kinds from roles.plan_artifact.kinds, which already exists in the vocabulary, so no keys were proposed. 'Authority commit', 'externally visible mutation', 'declared runtime execution' and 'journey' are ATDD journey-domain vocabulary (cf. urn.journey), not stack names, and were kept. Per-rule severity 3 / advisory disposition moved to core.verification per the notProfileKeys list. The reference to 'existing plan and source validators' names no validator ids and is described generically in core.verification.
